% A generated required argument is laid out the one way, whatever shape its
% value has: '{%' opens it so the newline behind the brace reaches TeX as
% nothing, and the closing brace sits on its own line. A comment inside the
% value can never reach that brace, so none of these needs a special case.
\cmd:::
    - plain
    - trailing % comment
    - 50\% off
    - % a whole line of comment
    -
        a continuation
        over two lines

% An explicit group is the author's own text, delimiters included, so only
% where the next argument starts is TeXFlux's to decide. An unescaped '%' on
% the group's last line sends it to the next line; without one it follows.
\pair:::
    + {authored % comment}
    - tail

\pair:::
    + {authored\% group}
    - tail

% A literal brace container opens the same way.
@{\small\color{gray}}::
    A block value inside a literal brace container.

\scalebox{0.9}::
    \input{figure.tex}%

% TeXFlux standard flow macros.
%
% These are ordinary source macros, seeded into every module environment by
% the compilation session. They manipulate structural flow only: nothing here
% knows a TeX command, so spacing and styling stay the author's own TeX.
%
% The names are frozen; section 9.1 of texflux_tex_first_dsl_v1_spec.md
% states what a new one would have to justify.

% Emit one value before a payload.
!defmacro{before}{prefix}{body}::
    !param{prefix}
    !param{body}

% Emit one value after a payload.
!defmacro{after}{suffix}{body}::
    !param{body}
    !param{suffix}

% Wrap a payload in a pair. Composable from !before and !after, and kept
% because a paired transformation is one conceptual operation.
!defmacro{around}{prefix}{suffix}{body}::
    !param{prefix}
    !param{body}
    !param{suffix}

% Drop one segment of a composition and keep the rest of the pipeline.
!defmacro{off}{ignored}{body}::
    !param{body}

% Discard a payload whole. The template is deliberately empty: a value that
% no template position reads contributes nothing.
!defmacro{drop}{body}::

that they behave like macros, that no module has to import them, and that the
module they come from stays invisible to authors and to external consumers.
